DeepSeek’s R1 release triggered the largest single-day loss in Nvidia's history because it demonstrated that a frontier-class, open-weights reasoning model could be trained for a fraction of incumbent costs, challenging the market thesis that AI capital expenditure and demand are moated by compute scale [Source: ev-1].

Specifically, DeepSeek released R1 on 2025-01-20 following its predecessor DeepSeek-V3 (released 2024-12-26), which reported training on roughly 2.79 million GPU-hours at a claimed cost of about US$5.6 million using export-restricted H800 chips [Source: ev-1]. On 2025-01/27, Nvidia lost approximately US$589 billion in market capitalization — the largest single-day loss in stock-market history at the time — with about US$1 trillion erased across the tech complex as markets repriced this thesis [Source: ev-1].

This efficiency revealed that scarcity driven by US export controls (specifically regarding H800 restrictions) forced Chinese labs to optimize economics rather than relying solely on massive compute budgets; thus, scarcity, not preference, drove these economic outcomes [Source: ev-1].
